solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Cure six-footer; to die otherwise (8)

indicatorNotes.otherwise: done otherwise, the letters of TO DIE come out in a different order

blocks.note: an insect has six legs, so an ant is a six-footer

annotation.surface: A grim remedy: cure the monster, or it dies.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' tempts you towards a tall person or a grave; here the feet are legs, and the six-legged creature is an insect.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a remedy that counteracts a poison cures its effects.

entries.clue: Demand on graduate from south somewhere in Scotland (8)

indicatorNotes.from south: in a down answer, read from the bottom up

annotation.surface: A graduate from the south makes demands in Scotland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'From south' sounds like someone's origin; in a down clue it means read upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a city in north-east Scotland.

entries.clue: Online travel firm has little about rent and cover (11)

indicatorNotes.about: the little word goes round the rent

blocks.note: a rent is a tear, a rip

annotation.surface: A travel company complaining about rent and insurance.
annotation.walkthrough: Rent and cover read as money matters, housing and insurance; they are a tear and a shade.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a website where travellers review hotels and restaurants, so an online travel firm.

entries.clue: “Bash rodents eating bread” is command (9)

indicatorNotes.eating: the rodents take the bread inside

blocks.note: a do or bash is a party
naan (also spelt nan) is Indian bread

annotation.surface: An order to hit the mice in the bread bin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bash' reads as a verb, to hit; it is a noun, a party, which a DO also is.
annotation.definitionFit: Command in the sense of mastery or control is dominance.

entries.clue: Liking head of nation to be brought down (5)

indicatorNotes.to be brought down: in a down answer, the letter moves lower in the column

blocks.clueFragment: head of nation to be brought down
blocks.note: the head of STATE, S, moves down two places

annotation.surface: Enjoying seeing a national leader toppled.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface topples a head of state; the actual job is to move the first letter of STATE down the column.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to have a fondness for jazz is to have a palate for it, a preference.

entries.clue: Duplicated recording containing single (6)

indicatorNotes.containing: the recording holds the other word inside it

blocks.note: CD, a compact disc recording: first half

annotation.surface: A studio note: the tape was copied, and it has the single on it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Single' reads as a pop record, fitting the recording; it is only the adjective, alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Cloned means copied exactly, duplicated.

entries.clue: Girl from France, the content of mural (5)

indicatorNotes.the content of: what is inside the word, without its ends

annotation.surface: A French girl painted in a wall picture.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface places a French girl in a painting; 'from France, the' just asks for the French word for 'the'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: any girl's first name will do for 'girl', and this is a common one, as in Petrarch's beloved.

entries.clue: Nothing to fasten bar back on camera (3)

indicatorNotes.bar: barring, except: leave that letter out
indicatorNotes.back on: the back letter of the next word

blocks.note: remove the last letter of camerA, A, from NAIL

annotation.surface: No way to fix a bar to the back of a camera.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a rod to be fastened; it means except, taking the A out of NAIL.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, most familiar from British football scores, where a side that fails to score has zero.

entries.clue: Old-fashioned son bound by moral obligation (5)

blocks.note: s = son, as in family trees

annotation.surface: An old-fashioned son tied by duty.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a description of a dutiful son; the definition sits at the front, and 'bound by' puts the son inside the obligation.
annotation.definitionFit: Dusty can mean dull and old-fashioned, as in a dusty answer.

entries.clue: Derision about irrational love for venomous type (8)

indicatorNotes.about: the derision wraps round the rest

annotation.surface: Mocking someone's senseless passion for a poisonous character.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Irrational love' reads as one idea, a mad passion; it is two pieces, the irrational number pi and O.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: an arachnid with a stinging tail, so a creature of the poisonous kind.

entries.clue: Recalled trap used in duplicate puzzles (7)

indicatorNotes.Recalled: called back, so the whole assembly runs backwards
indicatorNotes.used in: the trap is put inside the duplicate word

blocks.note: a gin is a snare or trap

annotation.surface: Someone recalls a trick used in paired puzzles.
annotation.walkthrough: GIN goes inside SAME to make SAMGINE, and 'Recalled' turns that whole string round. A gin trap is an old word for a snare.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: mysteries and riddles, things hard to work out.

entries.clue: Items snapped up close (7)

indicatorNotes.snapped: snapped like a twig, the letters of UP CLOSE are broken and reset

annotation.surface: Paparazzi snapping things close up.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a photographer's close-up. 'Items' in the gossip-column sense are couples who are dating.
annotation.definitionFit: Two people seen together romantically are an item, so several such pairs are items: couples.

entries.clue: Approached an errand drunkenly, having imbibed whiskey (5,4)

indicatorNotes.drunkenly: a drunk's letters stagger into a new order
indicatorNotes.having imbibed: the whiskey goes into the mix

blocks.note: Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Someone went out on a job after a few whiskies.
annotation.walkthrough: The whiskey sounds like the drink that caused the staggering; it is just the letter W, which joins the rearranged letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, as a phrasal verb: came closer, both in the past tense.

entries.clue: Cross whichever bridges lead to getting Romeo (5)

indicatorNotes.bridges: the word spans the other letters, holding them in its middle
indicatorNotes.lead to: the leading letter of the next word

blocks.note: ANY = whichever (any one you like): first two letters
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Advice on crossing any bridge that leads to Romeo.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like crossing a bridge, but it is the adjective meaning annoyed.
annotation.definitionFit: Cross and angry both mean annoyed.

entries.clue: Composer’s vault plagued with ghosts (6,5)

indicatorNotes.plagued with: troubled, so the letters are thrown into disorder

annotation.surface: A composer's tomb is haunted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Composer's' reads as possessive, whose vault; the 's is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the English writer of The Planets suite, one of many possible composers.

entries.clue: Third character dropped from team of fantastic folk (5)

indicatorNotes.Third character dropped from: take out the third letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: a football or cricket team is an ELEVEN; drop its third letter, E

annotation.surface: A player dropped from a team of fantasy characters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Third character' reads like the third player in a team sheet; it is the third letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Elven means belonging to elves, fantasy folk.

entries.clue: Enthusiasm when accepting relay with four going round (8)

indicatorNotes.accepting: to accept something is to take it in, so the word 'when' gives takes the relay and four inside itself
indicatorNotes.going round: the relay and four turn backwards

annotation.surface: Team spirit as four relay runners take a lap.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is athletics, with four runners going round; 'relay' is the verb to pass on, SEND, and 'four' is Roman IV.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the quality of being keen and eager.

entries.clue: Given a ship and one grand, returned home (8)

indicatorNotes.returned: sent back, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a den is a home or lair

annotation.surface: Someone got a ship and a thousand pounds and came back home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Returned home' reads as a sailor getting back; 'returned' only turns DEN round.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: allotted, as in 'given a task' or 'assigned a task'.

entries.clue: Dash around in square gathering tree’s first fruit (9)

indicatorNotes.around: turned around, so the dash runs backwards
indicatorNotes.in: the whole piece goes inside the square
indicatorNotes.gathering: the reversed dash takes the letter in
indicatorNotes.first: the tree's first is whatever comes first in the word tree, its opening letter

blocks.note: NINE, a square number (3 x 3): first letter
RACE = dash, turned around to ECAR: first two letters

annotation.surface: Rushing round a town square collecting a tree's first crop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Square' looks like a town square; it is a square number, NINE. The reversed dash holds T, and the lot goes inside NINE.
annotation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned peach, a fruit.

entries.clue: Steady sea ferries advanced fast (8)

indicatorNotes.ferries: the sea carries the other letters inside it

blocks.note: MED, the Mediterranean Sea: first two letters
a = advanced, as in A level
fast and sure both mean firm, secure

annotation.surface: A calm sea carries a speeding ship forward.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fast' reads as quick; here it means fixed or firm, as in hold fast.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a pace that is even and deliberate, unhurried and regular.

entries.clue: Introduces American woman with vice (6,2)

annotation.surface: Someone introducing a wicked American woman.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb phrase, so the answer is the two-word phrasal verb; 'with' simply joins the pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: To usher in is to introduce or bring in.

entries.clue: Crow and rook tucked into baked product (5)

indicatorNotes.tucked into: the rook goes inside the product

blocks.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook

annotation.surface: Two birds eating something baked.
annotation.walkthrough: The rook looks like the second bird; it is the chess piece. Crake is a dialect word for a crow.
annotation.definitionFit: In northern English dialect a crake is a crow or raven.

entries.clue: Game board art student covers (5)

indicatorNotes.covers: the words wrap round the answer

annotation.surface: A board game from an art student.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Game board' runs together as a board game; the break comes after 'Game', and the board is darts' own.
annotation.definitionFit: Darts is a pub game of throwing darts at a board.

entries.clue: Daughter finished port (5)

annotation.surface: A daughter has finished her port.
annotation.walkthrough: Port sounds like the drink the daughter finished; it is a harbour town. Dover is the English Channel ferry port.
annotation.definitionFit: Dover is a port on the south-east coast of England.

entries.clue: Be silent and mimic model (5)

annotation.surface: Advice to a quiet copycat model.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Model' reads as a noun, a fashion model; it is the verb, to form or shape.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: a sculptor who models clay forms it.

entries.clue: Try essentially dull remains after burning stews (9)

indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence, the core letters, of the word

blocks.note: have a go = have a try
ashes are what is left after a fire

annotation.surface: A burnt stew with dull leftovers.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the far end, and 'burning' makes it look like a kitchen failure.
annotation.definitionFit: Goulash is a Hungarian meat stew.

entries.clue: Not disheartened wearing uniform that is free (5)

indicatorNotes.disheartened: heart removed: the middle letter goes
indicatorNotes.wearing: the word is worn inside the others

blocks.note: Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet
NOT without its middle letter, O

annotation.surface: Someone cheerful in uniform, and so free.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not disheartened' reads as cheerful; it is the word NOT losing its heart.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: undoing a knot or rope frees whatever it held.

entries.clue: Veteran against eating bananas (7)

indicatorNotes.bananas: slang for crazy, so the letters go wild

annotation.surface: An old soldier refusing to eat bananas.
annotation.walkthrough: Bananas look like the food being eaten; 'bananas' is the rearranging signal and 'eating' is the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Veteran and vintage both describe something old and classic, as in a vintage or veteran car.

entries.clue: Fan that’s attached to bolt (3)

blocks.note: an enthusiast, a devotee: first sense
the threaded fastener screwed on to a bolt: second sense

annotation.surface: An admirer who never leaves someone's side.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' tempts as running away; it is the threaded rod.
annotation.definitionFit: A nut is both a fan and the part that fastens on a bolt.

entries.clue: One turning writerly almost finished novel (7)

indicatorNotes.almost finished: a word that is almost finished stops one letter short of its end
indicatorNotes.novel: new, so the letters take a new order

annotation.surface: A writer nearly done with a novel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Novel' and 'writerly' make a book; 'novel' is the rearranging signal, not the book.
annotation.definitionFit: A twirler is someone who twirls, one turning round.

entries.clue: Fairly despicable person snubbed present (6)

indicatorNotes.snubbed: cut short, like a snub nose, so the word loses its end

blocks.note: a rat is a despicable person
HERE = present, without its last letter

annotation.surface: A nasty person snubbed a gift.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift; it is HERE, present in the room.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as adverbs of degree: 'fairly cold' and 'rather cold' both mean somewhat cold.

entries.clue: Fault editor that’s gone to the opposition? (8)

annotation.surface: An editor at fault who has joined a rival paper.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: the editor who defected went over to the other side.
annotation.definitionFit: To defect is to desert to the opposing side.
